summary: Mobile IP rebinding causes duplicated mid-sentence fragments and missing stream tail on SSE/WS
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported repeated occurrences where SSE or WebSocket streaming sessions degrade when a mobile client experiences a network (IP) rebind (cellular <-> wifi or carrier NAT refresh). Symptom: during the reconnect the client sees duplicated mid-sentence fragments followed by the stream abruptly missing the final few sentences (tail) of the generation. The generated text shows overlapping tokens in the middle and a truncated ending, not a full duplicate of the entire stream.

Impact:
- Several Acme Analytics customers observed incorrect summary generation leading to data loss in downstream processing and usability regressions.
- Occurs intermittently on mobile networks; reproduces reliably for the customer when switching networks under load.
- Affects live inference customers on dedicated pools in us-east (P1 business impact).

Environment details:
- Customer: Acme Analytics (dedicated cluster)
- Region: us-east (prod)
- Frontdoor: internal load-balancer -> api-gateway (SSE/WS handling) -> sse-proxy -> serving runtime workers
- Client: Android app (Chrome WebView) and mobile Safari in some cases
- Models observed: gpt-open-7b, redwood-rl-13B
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Start a long streaming generation (>4KB) from mobile client on LTE.
2. While generation is in-flight, toggle network (disable cellular or switch to Wi-Fi) to force IP/port rebind.
3. Client reconnects to streaming endpoint using stored conversation token and resumes with a new socket.
4. Observe stream: mid-sentence tokens are repeated (duplicate fragment), then stream ends missing final 1-3 sentences.
5. Reproduce frequency increases when client has aggressive socket timeout and when LB session affinity is disabled.
logs:
[2026-03-12T13:22:11Z] sse-proxy: conn=abcd1234 client_ip=10.8.5.33 session_token=sess-xyz seq_start=1024
[2026-03-12T13:22:13Z] lb: conn-handoff client_old=10.8.5.33 client_new=100.64.12.7 path=/stream sess_token=sess-xyz
[2026-03-12T13:22:13Z] api-gateway: reconnect detected token=sess-xyz, ephemeral-port-change true
[2026-03-12T13:22:13Z] serving-runtime(worker-7): KV_CACHE_LOOKUP sess-xyz => found snapshot@offset=1100
[2026-03-12T13:22:13Z] serving-runtime(worker-7): started streaming from offset=1100 to client (new_conn=ef56)
[2026-03-12T13:22:13Z] sse-proxy: duplicate-fragment detected: seq=1135 content="...the model will" repeated
[2026-03-12T13:22:14Z] sse-proxy: stream-closed before end-marker, reason=client-abort (socket closed)
[2026-03-12T13:22:14Z] api-gateway: no explicit end event forwarded to client; worker marked completed
investigation:
Preliminary hypothesis: when the client rebinds IP, the load-balancer hands the new connection to a different proxy hop or the same worker but with a new ephemeral 5-tuple. The sse-proxy currently uses a short-lived in-memory session map keyed by socket address + session_token for optimization (fast-path). During rebind the fast-path mismatches and the worker attempts to 'resume' by resending from the last known offset. Due to race between prior in-flight fragments and resume stream, overlapping token ranges were emitted (duplicate mid-sentence). In some cases the final end-marker (stream end event) is lost because the downstream sse-proxy considered the session closed when the original socket went away, and the reconnect path didn't request a trailing suffix from the worker.

Reproduction: engineering reproduced locally with an Android emulator toggling cellular/Wi-Fi and with TCP half-close timing tuned. Repro is sensitive to client rebind timing and LB affinity settings.

Telemetry: added verbose seq and session_token logging to sse-proxy and serving-runtime. Found 17 distinct incidents for Acme Analytics in last 24 hours with the same footprint (seq overlap + missing end marker).

Related signals: existing tickets SUP-321999 and SUP-773319 show adjacent patterns (session drift, incomplete-final-chunk) but differ in root cause (proxy chunking vs auth-rotation).
workaround:
Short-term customer guidance:
- Advise client teams to treat reconnects as idempotent by implementing client-side merging: if duplicate fragments are received, dedupe by sequence numbers or timestamps.
- Increase client socket keepalive to reduce the chance of IP rebind during long streams.
- For critical tails, recommend using synchronous (non-streaming) finalization call: after stream completes on client, call /finalize to fetch the full assembled output.
- Server-side interim: enable LB session affinity for the dedicated cluster (sticky by session_token) to lower handoff probability.
resolution:
Planned fixes (tracked):
- Short term (next 48h): deploy sse-proxy patch to rely primarily on session_token for resume lookup (instead of socket 5-tuple) and to request missing end-suffix from worker on reconnect. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2421 (in review).
- Mid term (2 weeks): add reconcile protocol between sse-proxy and worker: on reconnect with same session_token, worker will compute whether a suffix was emitted and stream only the missing suffix; also add explicit end-marker ack path.
- Long term: add end-to-end test harness simulating IP rebinds and a telemetry metric (stream_resume_gap) to monitor regressions.

Status: sse-proxy fast patch deployed to staging and a hotfix candidate built; rollout to prod scheduled after smoke tests (target: 2026-03-16).
